title: Person-Centric Annotations of LAION-400M: Auditing Bias and Its Transfer to Models
claim: A multi-stage automatic labeling pipeline yields large-scale annotations that enable auditing dataset bias and its transfer to downstream models.
layout: Left-to-right flow in 3 stages, with analysis panel in a dashed rounded box at right
description: A wide left-to-right flow diagram. At left, a gray box lists an MLLM ensemble (InternVL, Qwen-VL, Phi-3.5-Vision, LLaVA-NeXT) with logos. An arrow leads into a dashed region with two rounded panels: a blue one of gender-labeled person crops (male, female, mixed, unclear) and a green one of race/ethnicity-labeled crops. A dark purple YOLO11 bounding-box box at the bottom feeds crops upward into both. The gender and race panels go to 'Train Gender/Race Classifier' blocks, then to 'Label Gender/Race in LAION-400M' blocks. A teal InternVL 'Person-Centric Captions' block sits below. All three feed into a dashed panel at right titled 'Auditing Dataset Bias and its Transfer to Models'. That panel holds small plots: crime-word boxplot, composition bars, race bars, SAE word lists, and CLIP and Stable-Diffusion scatter plots. Colors are blue for gender, green for race and teal for captions.
caption: We detect $\sim$200M person bounding boxes with YOLO11. An MLLM ensemble (Phi-3.5-Vision, LLaVA-NeXT, InternVL3) provides gender and race/ethnicity labels on sampled subsets, and only consensus predictions are used to train SigLIP classifiers. These classifiers then label the full dataset, while InternVL3 generates person-centric captions. The resulting annotations enable systematic analysis of dataset composition, harmful correlations, and bias transfer to downstream models. \revision{Images of people are regenerated from the originals by AI to protect privacy.}
abstract: Vision-language models trained on large-scale multimodal datasets show strong demographic biases, but the role of training data in producing these biases remains unclear. A major barrier has been the lack of demographic annotations in web-scale datasets such as LAION-400M. We address this gap by creating person-centric annotations for the full dataset, including over 276 million bounding boxes, perceived gender and race/ethnicity labels, and automatically generated captions. These annotations are produced through validated automatic labeling pipelines combining object detection, multimodal captioning, and finetuned classifiers. Using them, we uncover demographic imbalances and harmful associations, such as the disproportionate linking of men and individuals perceived as Black or Middle Eastern with crime-related and negative content. We also show that a linear fit predicts 60-70% of gender bias in CLIP and Stable Diffusion from direct co-occurrences in the data. Our resources establish the first large-scale empirical link between dataset composition and downstream model bias. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/LAION-400M-Person-Centric-Annotations.
